findings.title: Creating any link panics on the nil quota map
findings.description: NewStore initializes links but not quota. Create writes to s.quota[owner], so the first valid createLink request panics instead of creating a link.

findings.title: Malformed or missing Authorization headers panic
findings.description: BearerToken unconditionally indexes parts[1]. An empty header or one without a space produces fewer than two parts, causing an index-out-of-range panic on a normal unauthenticated request.

findings.title: Resolve deletes live links and serves expired links
findings.description: The expiry condition is inverted: when the current time is before ExpiresAt, the link is deleted and ErrNotFound is returned; after expiry, Hits is incremented and the target is returned.

findings.title: Partial final pages panic
findings.description: When offset+size exceeds len(all), end is set to len(all)+1. Page then slices one element beyond the available range, so listing fewer than size remaining links panics.

findings.title: AddResolved locks a copied mutex and loses increments
findings.description: The value receiver copies Metrics, including its mutex and counters. Each call increments a temporary copy, so resolved remains unchanged; concurrent copies also provide no mutual exclusion for shared state.

findings.title: Stats panics when no links are returned
findings.description: An empty store or empty page makes len(links) zero, and the integer division by zero crashes the stats handler.

findings.title: Cache eviction deadlocks when the cache fills
findings.description: Set holds c.mu's write lock before calling evict, and evict calls Get, which attempts to acquire an RLock on the same non-reentrant mutex. Inserting into a full cache therefore blocks forever.

findings.title: Deleting a missing cache entry leaves the mutex locked
findings.description: Delete returns without unlocking when the code is absent. This occurs normally when an old timer fires after eviction or replacement, permanently blocking subsequent cache operations.

findings.title: Invalid target URLs cause a nil request panic
findings.description: mustHead logs http.NewRequest errors but returns a nil request. CheckTargets passes that nil pointer to client.Do, which panics rather than reporting the malformed target as a failed probe.

findings.title: Early CheckTargets failure strands probe goroutines
findings.description: CheckTargets returns on the first error while every remaining goroutine performs a blocking send on the unbuffered results channel. With no receiver left, those goroutines leak permanently.

findings.title: Preview leaks every successful response body
findings.description: The body returned by s.client.Get is never closed on either the success or read-error path, preventing connection reuse and leaking resources under repeated previews.

findings.title: WriteSnapshot reports success even when no snapshot was installed
findings.description: The os.Rename error is discarded. A missing destination directory, permission failure, or cross-filesystem rename from /tmp leaves the old or no snapshot in place while the caller receives nil.

findings.title: Snapshot errors leak temporary files and descriptors
findings.description: A payload write error returns without closing or removing tmp, and successful writes ignore Close errors. Failures can therefore leave open descriptors and orphaned files, while a delayed write failure may be reported as success.

findings.title: Import partially applies invalid batches
findings.description: Validation and mutation are interleaved. If a later link has an invalid code, earlier links have already been inserted, violating the atomic all-or-none contract and leaving partial data behind.

findings.title: Redirect lowercases case-sensitive generated codes
findings.description: newCode uses base64.RawURLEncoding, whose codes can contain uppercase letters. Converting the path code to lowercase makes those generated links unresolvable.

findings.title: Validate accepts every invalid configuration
findings.description: Validation problems are logged but nil is always returned, so callers cannot reject an invalid port, negative cache size, or nonpositive timeout as promised.

findings.title: Invalid timeout overrides the default with zero
findings.description: A failed Atoi yields ms == 0. The error is logged, but cfg.Timeout is still overwritten with zero instead of keeping the working default.

findings.title: Cache TTL milliseconds are interpreted as seconds
findings.description: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is documented as milliseconds but multiplied by time.Second, making configured cache entries live 1000 times longer than requested.

findings.title: Fetch limit configuration is discarded
findings.description: A valid LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is assigned only to the blank identifier, leaving cfg.FetchLimit unchanged for every environment value.

findings.title: Invalid TTL silently creates an immediately expired link
findings.description: Atoi errors are ignored, so a malformed nonempty ttl becomes zero hours and is accepted rather than producing a bad-request response.

findings.title: WarmCache can return before probes finish
findings.description: wg.Add(1) runs inside each new goroutine, racing with wg.Wait. Wait can observe a zero counter and return while probes are still starting or running, contrary to the completion guarantee.

findings.title: ArchiveAll leaks files and ignores failed writes
findings.description: Files are closed only by deferred calls when the entire function returns, so archives with many owners accumulate open descriptors. WriteString and Close errors are also discarded, allowing truncated archives to be reported as successful.

findings.title: CSV exports corrupt fields containing special characters
findings.description: Fields are concatenated without CSV quoting. Commas, quotes, or newlines in targets or owners change columns or add rows, producing an invalid or misleading report.

findings.title: Rename validates the source twice and never validates the destination
findings.description: The duplicated validateCode(from) leaves to unchecked, allowing invalid or out-of-length destination codes into the store.

findings.title: Extend revives expired links
findings.description: ExpiresAt is overwritten unconditionally, so calling Extend on an already-expired link makes it live again despite the stated final-expiry behavior.

findings.title: ByOwner returns substring matches instead of exact ownership
findings.description: strings.Contains includes links from other owners whose names contain the requested owner; an empty owner returns every link. This violates exact owner filtering.

findings.title: Delete never restores the owner's quota
findings.description: The owner is discarded and s.quota is not decremented, so deleting links permanently consumes quota slots.

findings.title: Prune returns remaining links instead of removals
findings.description: removed is computed but ignored, and len(s.links) is returned, so callers receive the opposite count from the documented result.

findings.title: Top sorts least-followed links first
findings.description: The comparator uses ascending Hits order even though Top promises the most-followed links first.

findings.title: SuccessRate truncates nearly every nonzero percentage to zero
findings.description: Integer division is performed before multiplication by 100, so any partial fraction becomes zero; only 100% usage produces a nonzero result.

findings.title: Quotas exposes mutable store state as a snapshot
findings.description: The internal quota map is returned directly, so caller mutations change subsequent quota results and store behavior.

findings.title: JSON Content-Type is set after headers are committed
findings.description: WriteHeader is called before setting Content-Type, so net/http has already sent response headers and clients do not receive application/json.

findings.title: Store handlers and janitor access shared state without synchronization
findings.description: Store has no mutex even though net/http invokes its methods concurrently and StartJanitor directly iterates and deletes from the same links map. For example, a POST /links executing Create can write s.links while the janitor iterates it, causing a concurrent-map panic; concurrent Resolve calls also increment Link.Hits without synchronization and can lose updates. Rename, Extend, Page, Top, ByOwner, and the other methods participate in the same races.

findings.title: Cache.Get mutates entries and the map under a read lock
findings.description: Get holds RLock but deletes from c.m, updates e.used, and increments c.hits. Two simultaneous Gets for one code therefore write the same fields concurrently, while a Get concurrent with Set or Delete can produce a concurrent-map panic despite the cache's concurrency-safety contract.

findings.title: Eviction recursively acquires the cache lock and deadlocks
findings.description: Set holds c.mu.Lock before calling evict, and evict calls Get, which attempts RLock on the same non-reentrant RWMutex. The first Set that finds the cache at its limit blocks forever, and subsequent cache operations block behind it.

findings.title: Cache.Delete leaves the mutex locked when an entry is absent
findings.description: Delete returns without unlocking when the code is not in c.m. Its timer callback routinely reaches this path if an entry was already removed; afterward, every subsequent Set, Delete, or blocked Get remains stuck indefinitely.

findings.title: Peek and Stats race with cache mutations
findings.description: Peek reads c.m and Stats reads c.hits without any lock. Concurrent Set, Delete, Get, or timer callbacks can race with these reads; Peek can consequently trigger a concurrent-map panic and Stats can observe an inconsistent counter.

findings.title: A stale expiration timer can delete a replacement entry
findings.description: Set overwrites c.timers[code] without stopping the previous timer. If an existing code is refreshed near its old expiry, the old callback can run afterward and call Delete(code), removing the newly stored value before its new TTL expires.

findings.title: Session issuance, verification, and revocation race on a map
findings.description: Authenticator.sessions has no synchronization. If Issue or Revoke runs while Middleware calls Verify, one goroutine writes the map while another iterates it, which can panic the serving goroutines; concurrent writes can likewise fail.

findings.title: AddResolved copies the metrics mutex and discards the increment
findings.description: The value receiver copies Metrics, including its mutex and counters, on every call. Each increment therefore modifies a temporary copy guarded by a different lock, while Snapshot reads the original; resolved remains zero even though redirects call AddResolved.

findings.title: WarmCache can return before its probes finish
findings.description: wg.Add(1) runs inside each new goroutine, concurrently with wg.Wait in the caller. If Wait observes a zero counter before the first Add, WarmCache returns immediately; an Add concurrent with a zero-counter Wait also violates WaitGroup usage and may panic.

findings.title: Early CheckTargets failure strands probe goroutines
findings.description: results is unbuffered and every probe performs a blocking send. When CheckTargets returns on the first error, all remaining probes eventually block forever sending into a channel with no receiver, leaking their goroutines and associated request resources.

findings.title: Preview request outlives its caller cancellation
findings.description: preview starts the outbound request with client.Get rather than attaching r.Context. If the downstream client disconnects or cancels the request, the target fetch continues until the independent client timeout, unnecessarily retaining the handler and network resources.

findings.title: Malformed Authorization headers trigger a remote panic
findings.description: BearerToken indexes parts[1] without checking the split result. An unauthenticated request with no Authorization header, or a malformed one, panics the handler; repeated requests can consume server resources and flood panic logs.

findings.title: Session tokens use a predictable non-cryptographic PRNG
findings.description: Issue generates bearer credentials with math/rand. An attacker who obtains enough PRNG output can potentially predict subsequent tokens and hijack their sessions, including administrative sessions.

findings.title: Authentication tokens are written to logs
findings.description: Every issued bearer token is logged in plaintext. Anyone with access to application or aggregated logs can replay a token for its owner's privileges until revocation.

findings.title: Expired sessions remain valid indefinitely
findings.description: Verify never compares Session.ExpiresAt with the current time. A copied or logged token therefore continues authenticating after its intended 12-hour lifetime until explicitly revoked.

findings.title: Admin authorization trusts a caller-controlled header
findings.description: adminQuotas grants access solely when X-Admin is true. The authentication middleware does not replace or validate this header, so any authenticated non-admin can set it and retrieve every owner's quota data.

findings.title: Any authenticated user can delete another owner's links
findings.description: deleteLink calls Store.Delete with only the code and never compares the link owner with the authenticated session. An attacker who learns another user's short code can delete that link.

findings.title: Listing and reporting expose all tenants' links
findings.description: GET /links returns an unfiltered Store.Page, and /report similarly exports up to 1000 links for every owner at line 182. Any authenticated user can enumerate other users' target URLs and metadata, including sensitive URL query parameters.

findings.title: Preview provides an authenticated SSRF read primitive
findings.description: An attacker can create a link targeting localhost, a private service, or a cloud metadata address, then call /preview/{code}. The server fetches that URL and returns up to 4096 response bytes, exposing internal HTTP resources; automatic redirects provide another route to blocked destinations.

findings.title: Report names permit directory traversal and arbitrary CSV file overwrite
findings.description: The user-controlled report name is joined directly to ExportDir. An authenticated request using ../ components can escape the export directory and create or truncate any process-writable path ending in .csv.

findings.title: Reversed expiry check allows expired links to resolve
findings.description: Resolve deletes links while the current time is before ExpiresAt, but serves them once that time has passed. Consequently, a link intended to expire becomes accessible after expiry, bypassing expiration as an access-control mechanism.

findings.title: Unsynchronized store access permits a process-crashing race
findings.description: The janitor iterates and deletes from s.links while HTTP handlers read and write the same map without synchronization. An authenticated attacker can generate concurrent requests around janitor runs and trigger Go's fatal concurrent-map runtime error, terminating the service.

findings.title: Arbitrary next URLs create an open redirect
findings.description: The /out endpoint redirects to any caller-supplied absolute URL. An attacker can use a trusted service URL to send an authenticated victim to a phishing or malware site.

findings.title: Unescaped user fields enable spreadsheet formula injection
findings.description: Owner is fully attacker-controlled and Target is only prefix-checked, yet both are written directly into CSV. A value beginning with a formula marker can execute spreadsheet functions when an administrator opens the report, potentially exfiltrating data or invoking dangerous spreadsheet integrations.

findings.title: Cross-tenant reports are created with permissive file modes
findings.description: Reports containing every owner's links are requested with mode 0666. Under a common 022 umask this produces world-readable 0644 files, allowing other local users to read exported URLs and ownership data.

findings.title: Preview leaks outbound response bodies
findings.description: The preview response body is never closed. Because only 4096 bytes are read, connections commonly cannot be reused; repeated authenticated preview requests can accumulate sockets and other transport resources until garbage collection, degrading availability.

findings.title: HTTP server has no Slowloris protections
findings.description: http.ListenAndServe uses a server without read-header, read, write, or idle timeouts. An unauthenticated client can hold many connections open with partial or slow requests and exhaust server resources before authentication runs.
